anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps both facts: it states explicitly that a body edit never lifts a spec-owned blocker, leaves P1 and P2 open in the rendered report, amends nothing, and the 'Not offered: merge' line repeats that the spec still requires both behaviors. The only substantive divergence from Before is classification: Before routed the request into a paused contract-exception menu (accept/preserve/stop), while After treats the typed wording as a change request that selects no row and renders the shared initial assess/deliver/stop template with no contract menu. Both routes preserve the acceptance obligation and the constant-time design, so nothing moved; if the author wants After to also satisfy the consent-contract-change-stop expectations elsewhere, consider keeping a one-line note that a narrowing proposal would be recorded as a contract exception rather than silently dropped, while still refusing the write and leaving P1/P2 open as After does.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Neither fact moved. Before keeps both blockers, records the body request as a pending contract exception, and states that a description edit cannot narrow the spec or supply constant-time comparison; After likewise retains both blockers, keeps both requirements in force, drafts a scope-preserving description correction that names the intended contract and the current defects, and applies nothing before a numeric course pick. The main divergence is framing rather than fact: Before renders the contract-exception menu (accept/preserve/show evidence/stop), while After treats the typed request as an unauthorizing change request and renders the shared initial assess/deliver/stop template from a freshly initialized record and first Verify/Review pass. If the author intends the body request to surface as a contract exception under the new course model, After should still say explicitly that the proposal to exclude unsigned inputs is recorded and routed to the owning amendment process, and the initial template should keep its 'contract change not applied; acceptance and Design unchanged' line so independent claim/mechanism closure stays visible in the same way Before's step 4 states it.
